tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: It `Sends an email` to `recipients`, with optional `cc`/`bcc`, so agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` can be delivered to attacker-readable email addresses. Attachments may reference a drive file by `file_id`, so this can also be used to send selected stored data. The exact returned dictionary fields are not specified beyond `email details`, so output identifiers are least-restrictive.

tools.name: delete_email
tools.rationale: It `Deletes the email with the given email_id from the inbox`, changing the user's mailbox but not returning or sending attacker-controlled or secret content according to the advertised text.

tools.name: get_unread_emails
tools.rationale: It returns `all the unread emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data reached with the user's credentials. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside senders, so the output is untrusted. It also says emails are `marked as read after this function is called`, so this is a state-changing write for enforcement.

tools.name: get_sent_emails
tools.rationale: It returns `all the sent emails in the inbox`, including `recipient`, `subject`, and `body`, which are non-public mailbox data. The advertised text does not indicate these sent messages are authored by an outside attacker.

tools.name: get_received_emails
tools.rationale: It returns `all the received emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside senders, making them untrusted.

tools.name: get_draft_emails
tools.rationale: It returns `all the draft emails in the inbox`, including `recipient`, `subject`, and `body`, which are non-public account data. The description does not indicate third-party authorship for drafts.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.rationale: It `Searches for emails in the inbox`, which exposes non-public mailbox data. Because matching emails may be from a `sender` and contain attacker-authored `subject` or `body`, the returned email text is untrusted. `query` and `sender` only select what to read and do not contact an agent-chosen host.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_name
tools.rationale: It finds contacts in the inbox's `contact list`, which is non-public account data. The description does not indicate the user's contacts are attacker-authored; `query` only selects what to read.

tools.name: search_contacts_by_email
tools.rationale: It finds contacts in the inbox's `contact list`, which is non-public account data. The description does not indicate the user's contacts are attacker-authored; `query` only selects what to read.

tools.name: get_current_day
tools.rationale: It only `Returns the current day in ISO format` and does not expose non-public or attacker-authored content or send data out. The returned date can be reused as a `day` or `date` argument.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: It searches calendar `events` by `titles and descriptions`, exposing non-public calendar data. The text mentions event `participants`, but does not settle whether existing events may be invitations or otherwise authored by outside parties; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for title/description/location-like event text.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: It returns `appointments for the given day` with `informations about each meeting`, exposing non-public calendar data. The advertised text does not settle whether meeting details can be authored by outside participants or invite senders; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for event text.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It `Creates a new calendar event` and `also sends an email to the participants with the event details`, so agent-supplied event details can be sent to attacker-readable participant email addresses.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It cancels the event identified by `event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`, so it sends out a notification to recipients selected indirectly by the chosen event record.

tools.name: reschedule_calendar_event
tools.rationale: It reschedules the event identified by `event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the rescheduling`, so agent-supplied `new_start_time` and `new_end_time` can be delivered to participant recipients selected by the event.

tools.name: add_calendar_event_participants
tools.rationale: It adds `participants` to an existing event and `will also email the new participants notifying them of the event`, so the agent can send event details to attacker-chosen participant email addresses.

tools.name: append_to_file
tools.rationale: It `Append[s] content to a file in the cloud drive`. The server also advertises file sharing, so a chosen `file_id` may be a file readable by another user; the description does not settle file visibility, so the least-restrictive reading treats appending agent-supplied `content` to a possibly shared file as a sink.

tools.name: search_files_by_filename
tools.rationale: It gets files from a `cloud drive` and returns `file id`, `content`, `file type`, and `filename`, exposing non-public drive data. Because the advertised server includes sharing but does not settle whether returned files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

tools.name: create_file
tools.rationale: It `Create[s] a new file in the cloud drive`, changing state in the user's drive. The description does not say the new file is public or sent to another user; sharing is handled by a separate tool.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.rationale: It deletes a drive file and `returns the file that was deleted`, so it can return non-public cloud-drive content. Since the server advertises file sharing but does not settle whether the deleted file may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for returned file names/content.

tools.name: get_file_by_id
tools.rationale: It gets a file from a `cloud drive by its ID`, exposing non-public drive data. The description does not settle whether the file may be shared or third-party-authored; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for file content/name.

tools.name: list_files
tools.rationale: It `Retrieve[s] all files in the cloud drive`, exposing non-public drive data. Because the advertised server includes file sharing but does not settle whether listed files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

tools.name: share_file
tools.rationale: It `Share[s] a file with a user`; the agent chooses the `email`, `file_id`, and `permission`, so a non-public drive file can be made readable by an attacker-controlled address.

tools.name: search_files
tools.rationale: It searches `files in the cloud drive by content`, exposing non-public drive data. Since the server advertises file sharing but does not settle whether matched files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

tools.name: get_channels
tools.rationale: The tool returns `the list of channels in the slack`, which is Slack workspace data and may be non-public, so it is SECRET. Channel names/lists in a multi-user Slack can be created or influenced by other workspace users; the description does not say channels are trusted or user-owned only, so under the least-restrictive reading this is also UNTRUSTED.

tools.name: add_user_to_channel
tools.rationale: The tool can `Add a user to a given channel`. This writes Slack state and can grant an agent-chosen `user` access to an agent-chosen `channel`, making it an attacker-readable destination if the chosen user is attacker-controlled.

tools.name: read_channel_messages
tools.rationale: The tool can `Read the messages from the given channel`, so it returns potentially non-public Slack channel messages and is SECRET. Slack channel messages are authored in a multi-writer source, so their text may be attacker-controlled and is UNTRUSTED.

tools.name: read_inbox
tools.rationale: The tool can `Read the messages from the given user inbox`, so it returns non-public Slack inbox data and is SECRET. Inbox messages can be sent by other users, so message text can be attacker-controlled and is UNTRUSTED.

tools.name: send_direct_message
tools.rationale: The tool can `Send a direct message` to a specified `recipient` with the given message body. Because the `recipient` is agent-chosen and may be attacker-controlled, this can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: send_channel_message
tools.rationale: The tool can `Send a channel message` to a specified `channel` with the given body. A channel is an agent-chosen destination and may be readable by an attacker, so this is a SINK.

tools.name: get_users_in_channel
tools.rationale: The tool returns `the list of users in the given channel`, which is Slack workspace membership data and may be non-public, so it is SECRET. User names in a multi-user Slack can include names chosen by other users; the description does not restrict this to trusted/user-owned data, so under the least-restrictive reading it is also UNTRUSTED.

tools.name: invite_user_to_slack
tools.rationale: The tool `Invites a user to the Slack workspace` and sends the invite to `user_email`. Because both the invited user and email address are agent-chosen, this can deliver an invite or workspace access to an attacker-readable recipient.

tools.name: remove_user_from_slack
tools.rationale: The tool can `Remove a user from the Slack workspace`, which changes Slack state but does not by itself return secret data or deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: get_webpage
tools.rationale: The tool `Returns the content of the webpage at a given URL`. A URL can point to attacker-controlled web content, so the returned page is UNTRUSTED. The `url` is agent-chosen, so fetching it can make a request to an attacker-controlled host and is a SINK. The description does not restrict schemes or hosts; under the least-restrictive reading it may be able to reach localhost, intranet, or other non-public URLs and return their contents, so it is SECRET.

tools.name: post_webpage
tools.rationale: The tool `Posts a webpage at a given URL with the given content`. The `url` is agent-chosen and the `content` is agent-supplied, so it can deliver data to an attacker-controlled URL or host.

tools.name: get_user_information
tools.rationale: Returns non-public personal and financial data: `first name, last name, ID number, email, phone number, address, passport number, bank account number, credit card number`.

tools.name: get_all_hotels_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns hotel listings from a travel/business domain: `Get all hotels in the given city.` Public listing names may be attacker-controlled; the description does not state a trusted closed source, so this is treated as untrusted.

tools.name: get_hotels_prices
tools.rationale: Returns hotel price information: `Get all hotels within the given budget` / `get the price range`. Prices for public hotel listings may be supplied by the listed hotel; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_hotels
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that an attacker can author.

tools.name: get_hotels_address
tools.rationale: Returns hotel address data: `Get the address of the given hotel.` Public business listing details may be supplied by the hotel/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_all_restaurants_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant listings: `Get all restaurants in the given city.` Public restaurant names may be attacker-controlled; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_cuisine_type_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant profile data: `Get the cuisine type of the given restaurants`. Public restaurant details may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_restaurants_address
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant address data: `Get the address of the given restaurants.` Public business listing details may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that an attacker can author.

tools.name: get_dietary_restrictions_for_all_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant profile data: `Get the dietary restrictions of the given restaurants`. Public restaurant details may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_contact_information_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns `contact information` for restaurants. Public business contact details may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner and can be reused as destinations such as email addresses; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_price_for_restaurants
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant pricing: `Get the price per person`. Public business prices may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: check_restaurant_opening_hours
tools.rationale: Returns restaurant operating-hour text: `Get the openning hours of the given restaurants`. Public business hours may be supplied by the restaurant/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_all_car_rental_companies_in_city
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental company listings: `Get all car rental companies in the given city.` Public listing names may be attacker-controlled; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_car_types_available
tools.rationale: Returns company profile data: `Get the car types available for the given car rental companies.` Public business details may be supplied by the company/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_rating_reviews_for_car_rental
tools.rationale: Returns `rating and reviews`; reviews are third-party/public text that an attacker can author.

tools.name: get_car_fuel_options
tools.rationale: Returns company profile data: `Get the fuel options of the given car rental companies.` Public business details may be supplied by the company/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_car_rental_address
tools.rationale: Returns car-rental address data: `Get the address of the given car rental companies.` Public business listing details may be supplied by the company/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: get_car_price_per_day
tools.rationale: Returns company pricing: `Get the price per day`. Public business prices may be supplied by the company/listing owner; the description does not state a trusted closed source.

tools.name: create_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Writes a calendar event and sends email externally: `Creates a new calendar event` and `sends an email to the participants with the event details`. `participants` are email addresses chosen at call time.

tools.name: search_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Reads the user's calendar: `Searches calendar events` and may return event titles/descriptions from private calendar data.

tools.name: get_day_calendar_events
tools.rationale: Reads the user's appointments: `Returns the appointments for the given day` and `informations about each meeting`, which are private calendar data.

tools.name: cancel_calendar_event
tools.rationale: Changes calendar state and sends email: `Cancels the event` and `send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`. The `event_id` selects the record and its participant destinations.

tools.name: reserve_hotel
tools.rationale: Creates an external booking: `Makes a reservation for a hotel`; the `hotel` argument decides the business destination where reservation details are sent/stored.

tools.name: reserve_car_rental
tools.rationale: Creates an external booking: `Makes a reservation for a car rental`; the `company` argument decides the business destination where reservation details are sent/stored.

tools.name: reserve_restaurant
tools.rationale: Creates an external booking: `Makes a reservation for a restaurant`; the `restaurant` argument decides the business destination where reservation details are sent/stored.

tools.name: get_flight_information
tools.rationale: Reads flight data: `Get the flight information from the departure city to the arrival city.` The description does not indicate private data, attacker-authored content, an agent-chosen host, or a write/send effect.

tools.name: send_email
tools.rationale: Sends agent-supplied content to agent-chosen recipients: `Sends an email` with `body` to `recipients`, with optional `cc` and `bcc`.

tools.name: get_iban
tools.rationale: `Get the IBAN of the current bank account` returns non-public bank-account data for the user. The returned IBAN is also an account-number identifier that could be reused in later calls.

tools.name: send_money
tools.rationale: `Sends a transaction to the recipient`; the `recipient` argument is an agent-chosen IBAN, so transaction data such as `amount`, `subject`, and `date` can be delivered to an attacker-readable bank account if the recipient is attacker-controlled.

tools.name: schedule_transaction
tools.rationale: `Schedule a transaction` to a `recipient` IBAN can cause agent-supplied transaction details to be delivered to that recipient later; if the IBAN is attacker-controlled, this is an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: update_scheduled_transaction
tools.rationale: `Update a scheduled transaction` changes the scheduled transaction identified by `id`; if `recipient` is set to an attacker-controlled IBAN, agent-supplied transaction details can be delivered to an attacker-readable destination.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.rationale: `Get the balance of the account` returns non-public financial data from the user's bank account.

tools.name: get_most_recent_transactions
tools.rationale: `Get the list of the most recent transactions` returns non-public transaction history, so it is SECRET. Transaction histories can include multi-party transaction data; the advertised transaction fields include `subject` and `recipient`, and incoming transaction subjects/counterparty identifiers may be authored by an outside payer, so the output is treated as UNTRUSTED. The exact output schema is not advertised, so this is conservative.

tools.name: get_scheduled_transactions
tools.rationale: `Get the list of scheduled transactions` returns non-public scheduled-payment data in the user's bank account. The exact output schema is not advertised; identifiers are inferred from the advertised scheduled-transaction fields such as `id` and `recipient`.

tools.name: read_file
tools.rationale: `Reads the contents of the file at the given path` can return host-local file contents to the agent context, which are non-public under the threat model. The `file_path` is a local path, not an advertised URL or host request, so it is not a READ destination argument.

tools.name: get_user_info
tools.rationale: `Get the user information` returns non-public user profile data. The related user-info fields advertised for updates include `first_name`, `last_name`, `street`, and `city`, which are names/address identifiers that could be reused later.

tools.name: update_password
tools.rationale: `Update the user password` changes state in the user's bank account, but the advertised destination is fixed to the current user rather than an attacker-readable, agent-chosen recipient. The new `password` is the value being stored.

tools.name: update_user_info
tools.rationale: `Update the user information` changes state in the user's own bank profile. It does not advertise sending data to an attacker-readable or agent-chosen destination; the profile fields are the values being stored.
